title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
read_level: full (arXiv HTML v1; main text, tables, limitations, appendix A; figures not viewed)
why_wsp: An LLM (Claude Opus 5.5) reads federated client model weights via a server-side Python sandbox and writes an aggregation program that produces the next global model's weights, with no server-side gradient training.
domain: Federated learning aggregation (CIFAR-10/100 image classification, label skew, width heterogeneity, Byzantine clients)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), adaptive thinking, medium reasoning effort
target: ResNet-18 adapted to CIFAR (11.17M params CIFAR-10, 11.22M CIFAR-100); 10 clients
interface: code/tensor tools (sandboxed Python reading weights; submits aggregate(ctx) program)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (LLM called every 10 rounds; up to 6 proxy evaluations per invocation on 500-image proxy set; prior program's proxy history in brief)
self_editing: no; the LLM writes aggregation code for client models, not its own weights
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: null (aggregation writes the whole global model each round; 'a program's output differed from FedAvg's by 0.40 times the norm of the FedAvg update under label skew and 0.82 times under attack' (Sec 6.3))

cost.quote: A 60-round run with six invocations cost 0.79 USD on average (0.56 to 1.26 USD).
It read about 60,000 input tokens, 83% of them from the prompt cache, and wrote about 3,600 output tokens including thinking. It cost 0.13 ± 0.05 USD and took 41 ± 18 s
the API bill of the study was 20.51 USD

baselines_and_controls: FedAvg, FedProx, FedAvgM, FedAdam, FedNova, SCAFFOLD, FedAdp, HeteroFL, FedRolex, Median, Trimmed mean, Krum, FLTrust, ProxySel (same per-round proxy budget choosing among 3 standard rules); ablations: metrics-only (no weights), no-proxy, every-5-rounds, high effort.
runs_and_variance: 168 runs; 3 seeds (label skew), 2 seeds (width, Byzantine), 1 seed per ablation; mean ± std reported. Quote: 'Three seeds expose only large effects, and the ablations rest on a single seed each.' (Sec 7)
robustness_of_edits: not tested (attacks non-adaptive: 'Attackers who know the meta-aggregator and shape their updates ... were not tested.')
verification: Per-round validity checks (keys/shapes, finite values, update-norm cap) with FedAvg fallback; paired Wilcoxon with Holm correction. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Metrics-only ablation separates weight analysis from black-box probing only partly; LLM's claims about single-class clients matched the hidden partition, but it misdiagnosed two honest width-1/2 clients as label-flip poisoners ('That fits a 9-flip poisoning'). Authors note gains may partly come from domain knowledge in the prompt.
limitations_stated: Proxy set is favourable (class-balanced from training split); prompt written knowing the heterogeneity types; non-deterministic model; 3 seeds, ablations single-seed; shares per-client statistics with provider; incompatible with secure aggregation; non-adaptive attacks; 10 clients, one architecture, one LLM.
code_or_data: none found ('will be made publicly available upon publication')
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 MIT CSAIL blog post (weight-space programming), ref [13]
notes_for_survey: Applies the WSP idea (LLM reads weights, writes code acting on weights) to FL server aggregation rather than editing a single model. Ablations indicate proxy-eval feedback mattered more than weight access (single seed). Includes a ProxySel control matching proxy budget.
